learning_objective: 🎯 Understand how substances magically transform into new materials, and learn the mathematical art of balancing chemical equations!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Due to the Law of Conservation of Mass, the number of atoms of each element must remain the same before and after a chemical reaction. We balance equations by adding coefficients (like 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O).
Combination: Two or more substances combine to form a single product (A + B → AB). Decomposition: A single reactant breaks down into simpler products using heat, light, or electricity (AB → A + B).

Single Displacement: A more reactive element kicks out a less reactive element from its compound. Double Displacement: Two compounds exchange their ions to form two new compounds (often forming a solid precipitate).
Oxidation is the gain of oxygen or loss of hydrogen. Reduction is the loss of oxygen or gain of hydrogen. When both happen simultaneously, it's a Redox reaction.
Corrosion is the slow eating away of metals by air and moisture (like rusting of iron). Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils in food, causing a bad smell and taste.

fun_activity.title: 🍎 The Apple Oxidation Test
fun_activity.instructions: Cut an apple in half. Leave one half on the table and rub lemon juice (an antioxidant) on the other half. Check back in an hour. The plain half turned brown due to Oxidation! The lemon juice protected the other half.

exam_tips: 📌 Always write the physical states (s, l, g, aq) of reactants and products to make the equation more informative.
📌 Remember that Respiration is an exothermic reaction (it releases energy), while Photosynthesis is endothermic (it absorbs sunlight).
📌 Learn the definition of a 'Precipitate' (an insoluble solid that emerges from a liquid solution).
quick_recap: ⭐ A chemical equation is a shorthand representation of a chemical reaction using symbols and formulas.
⭐ Heating calcium carbonate (limestone) to get quicklime is a classic thermal decomposition reaction.
⭐ Flushing bags of chips with Nitrogen gas prevents the oil from oxidizing and becoming rancid.
